question.problem:
Compute $P(X<2)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{225}({x}^{3}-x),\, & 1\le x\le 4, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a\le X<b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is identical to zero for all $x<1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<2) & ={\int }_{1}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{4}{225}({x}^{3}-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{4}{225}{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{3}-x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{4}{225}{[\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{4}{225}([\frac{1}{4}(2)^{4}-\frac{1}{2}(2)^{2}]-[\frac{1}{4}(1)^{4}-\frac{1}{2}(1)^{2}]) \\  & =\frac{4}{225}(4-2-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{4}{225}\cdot \frac{9}{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$
